editorial: You know the Ted Bundy story, but this movie shows it from a side you rarely see. Instead of focusing on the murders, it follows Elizabeth Kloepfer, the woman who loved him and refused to believe he was a killer. Zac Efron plays Bundy with a charming smile that makes you understand why so many people trusted him. Lily Collins gives a quiet, heartbreaking performance as a woman slowly waking up to the truth. The movie moves at a steady pace, jumping between their relationship and the courtroom drama that made Bundy famous. It is not a gory true crime film, which some viewers might find refreshing, while others may want more detail about the actual crimes. The courtroom scenes are tense and well acted, and the film keeps you guessing about how much Elizabeth really knew. If you enjoy character driven crime dramas, this one is worth your time. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or pick up the 4K Blu-ray for your collection.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Bundy is on trial and Elizabeth finally visits him in prison. She asks him directly if he killed those women, and he finally admits it by nodding. She walks away, heartbroken but free. The movie ends with real footage of Bundy's execution and a list of his victims, reminding you that behind the charm was a real monster. Elizabeth moves on with her life, finally letting go of the man she thought she knew.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves true crime stories and character driven dramas.
